conceptZh: 玩具機器人用吸管喝水，越吸越用力，臉頰整個凹下去，最後「啵」一聲整個杯子吸黏在他臉上拔不下來；他頂著杯子面無表情地站著，然後乾脆頂著杯子走掉。
object: a small toy robot and a chunky cup with a bendy straw
morph: the glyph 喝 stands still as a solid sculpture while the suction gag plays out beside it
creativeAngle: 喝水是生活常用字，笑點用「吸太用力把杯子吸在臉上」這個孩子自己也試過的身體笑話，收在他若無其事頂著杯子走掉更好笑。喝為口部加曷共十二畫，右邊橫畫多容易糊，字體靜止並要求橫畫等距。語音詞「喝水」，水ㄕㄨㄟˇ已學過，喝在此念ㄏㄜ，避開喝采的ㄏㄜˋ。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 喝 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep teal, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the 口 radical on the left and the 曷 component on the right stay clearly separated, with every horizontal stroke inside 曷 evenly spaced and never merging. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. Beside its lower left stands a small boxy toy robot holding a chunky cup with a bendy straw. From 0.6 seconds he starts to drink, and immediately overdoes it: his cheeks hollow inwards, his shoulders rise, the straw squeaks, and the whole cup visibly deforms as he pulls harder and harder. At 2.2 seconds there is a soft pop and the cup seals itself flat against his face, covering it entirely. He goes completely still, a robot with a cup for a head. Beat. At 3.0 seconds he tries once to pull it off with both hands, the cup stretches his face forward and snaps back, and he gives up immediately. At 3.8 seconds he simply straightens up, adjusts the cup as if it were a smart hat, and strolls calmly out of frame to the left by 4.6 seconds. From 4.7 seconds to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 喝 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「喝、喝、喝水」, using the reading ㄏㄜ for 喝 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 喝 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 喝水 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 喝: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 玩具戰士一劍揮倒一排杯子，連鎖倒下的彩色杯子剛好排成「喝」，戰士咕嚕咕嚕喝水。
object: a chunky toy warrior with a foam sword and a round shield, and a row of tumbling paper cups in turquoise
morph: a long chain of turquoise cups tumbles and lands in the shape of the glyph 喝
creativeAngle: 骨牌效應：戰士英勇一揮，杯子骨牌倒成「喝」；「喝水」用最後一杯水被他仰頭灌下去呼應。
promptEn: An 8-second bold-and-silly cartoon clip on a clean solid pale rose backdrop, with one large Traditional Chinese glyph 喝 as the only text, formed from thick glossy saturated turquoise cups and tubes laid flat as strokes, about 70% of frame height, centered and uncropped. Lead: a chunky toy warrior with a foam sword and a round shield, all bravado and very little skill; one supporting object, a pitcher of water with a bendy straw. No background music, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Voice: warm, friendly off-screen narrator in clear Taiwanese Mandarin saying exactly 喝、喝、喝水 (ㄏㄜ、ㄏㄜ、ㄏㄜ ㄕㄨㄟˇ), slowly with clear tones, then silence. Moment 1 (0–1.7s): the warrior marches in banging his shield with the foam sword, strikes a heroic pose in front of a tall zigzag line of upright turquoise cups, and as the first 喝 is spoken he taps the first cup with his sword tip, tink. Moment 2 (1.7–3.4s): the cups fall in a rolling wave and he leaps ahead, running along the line trying to stand them back up, his shield banging on the floor; one cup spins on its rim and bonks his helmet and he spins twice, stars-like sparkles circling. Moment 3 (3.4–5s): he throws up his hands, and the cups finish tumbling by themselves, curling around a corner and settling with a clatter as the second 喝 is spoken: a small square mouth shape on the left, and on the right a flat top bar over a boxed face with a hooked tail below. Moment 4 (5s): the word 喝水 is spoken as the warrior grabs the pitcher, upends it, and his cheeks balloon with water as he gulps with exaggerated glug motions, a few droplets bouncing off his shield. Final 5–8s: the glyph 喝 remains perfectly still, cups and tubes flat and neat, while the warrior beside it wipes his mouth, shakes his sword in triumph, and bounces on his heels, never touching any cup. Soft daylight, no flashing, no real people, no other text.
